text:
The Kings are 9-12-2 and deserve better, which is cold comfort in a division race. Our numbers say Los Angeles has earned about 25 points on its chances and has 20, one of the bigger gaps in the league. Peter Laviolette's team gets 51% of the expected goals; it has scored about five fewer goals than its chances say and allowed about seven more.

The good version of this team is easy to see. Artemi Panarin, back from injury on Monday with an assist, plays with Adrian Kempe and Alex Laferriere on a line that has 62% of the expected goals and a 9-3 goal edge. Darcy Kuemper, who has now played 500 NHL games, stopped 29 shots in Monday's 2-1 win over Montreal in Dylan Larkin's Canadiens debut. Drew Doughty played his 1,300th game with the Kings, a milestone ClutchPoints noted puts him alongside Nicklas Lidstrom in NHL history.

The worry is depth and the blue line. Erik Gustafsson is out two to four weeks with a hand fracture (Daily Faceoff), which breaks up the Kings' best pair (Gustafsson and Brandt Clarke, 58% of the expected goals). The second line of Mats Zuccarello, Kevin Fiala and Quinton Byfield gets only 39%.

Our numbers give Los Angeles a 37% chance at the playoffs. What we'd watch: whether the finishing evens out over the next month, because the Kings have played four or five fewer games than some rivals and the process says they can still climb.
